newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 26.

text.p: There are 97 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said the Beijing visit of U.S. Vice President Al Gore proved that Americans should go to China to see what the country was really like, which was far more effective than believing in the wrong image of China portrayed by the Western media.

-- The ECONOMIC TIMES said the United States had sent China a clear message expressing its wish to maintain a stable and constructive relationship, and now it was up to China to respond. It said whether China could retain its Most Favoured Nations trading status or join the World Trade Organisation may cause some fluctuations but would not be major obstacles in the development of bilateral relations.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said Xinhua News Agency's promise not to interfere with the internal affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region after the handover was positive but not enough. It said the agency should also promise not to secretly mobilise people to influence Hong Kong internal affairs. If the Chinese Communist Party wanted to operate in the territory, it had to set up a Hong Kong office and operate legally and openly, the paper said.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD said that patience for an agreement on the issue of the right of abode was wearing thin among Hong Kong people and members of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group. Time was running out and the paper said the JLG should solve the issue immediately.
